deck: LineCrew Pro Complete Feature and Role Training

slides.title: LineCrew Pro
slides.script: Welcome to LineCrew Pro, a field operations platform built for powerline contractors. This training explains the complete workflow, then walks through the exact responsibilities of Foremen, General Foremen, and company Administrators. You will see how safety, contract pricing, jobs, daily production, approvals, storm work, and reporting connect without mixing one contractor's data with another.

slides.title: Everything LineCrew Pro Connects
slides.script: LineCrew Pro connects six major parts of the operation. Company setup controls users and roles. Pricing manages customers, contracts, and price books. Jobs organize utility packets and work points. Field workflows capture morning safety and daily production. Review tools control approvals, redlines, and audit history. Storm Mode adds event and crew tracking without interrupting normal work.

slides.title: One Workflow, Three Levels of Responsibility
slides.script: The workflow follows the real workday. A Foreman completes the morning JSA, leads the crew, and records production at the end of the day. A General Foreman reviews submitted work and resolves exceptions. An Administrator controls company settings, pricing, imports, final approvals, reporting, and storm configuration. Each person sees the tools and pricing appropriate for their role.

slides.title: Company Data Stays Separate
slides.script: LineCrew Pro is designed as a multi-tenant commercial system. Every customer, contract, price book, job, report, and safety record belongs to one company. Supabase row-level security and server-side functions enforce that ownership. Screen permissions improve usability, but the database rules provide the real protection against one contractor viewing or changing another contractor's information.

slides.title: Contracts and Price Books
slides.script: Customers and utilities are created first. Contracts are then tied to the correct customer, with contract numbers, dates, notes, and active status. Each price book belongs to a contract and company. Administrators can use actual contract pricing and, when desired, set an adjusted field percentage so Foremen see a controlled production value while General Foremen and Administrators can compare both amounts.

slides.title: Price Book Operations
slides.script: Create the original price book, then duplicate it whenever revised pricing is issued. This preserves historical versions instead of overwriting old rates. Units can be entered manually or imported from common spreadsheet formats. Column mapping handles unfamiliar utility headings. The preview identifies problems before saving. After import, use search, category filters, status controls, editing, and CSV export to manage large books efficiently.

slides.title: Jobs, Utility Packets, and Work Points
slides.script: A job connects the customer, utility, contract, and field activity. Administrators can attach a utility job package containing work points, unit codes, and authorized quantities. Labels such as eighteen, Pole eighteen, and W P eighteen are normalized for matching. Production entered before the packet arrives remains valid and reconciles later. Progress displays authorized, reported, approved, and remaining work.

slides.title: Fast Daily Production Entry
slides.script: The Foreman can enter production for several poles and multiple units on one daily report. Ten lines are available immediately, with more lines on demand. Begin typing a unit code or description. Exact code matches appear first, and frequently used units rise in the results over time. Select the pole, Install or Remove, enter the quantity, and save all completed lines together.

slides.title: Authorized, Pending Packet, and Redline
slides.script: Every reported unit receives a review status. Authorized means the unit and quantity match the utility packet at that location. Pending Packet means production was recorded before a package was available and will reconcile later. Redline means the unit or quantity falls outside the current authorization. These statuses allow work to continue while giving management clear exception control.

slides.title: Morning JSA
slides.script: The morning JSA is separate from the end-of-day production report. Before work begins, the Foreman selects the work context, documents the plan, identifies hazards, records controls, required P P E, and the emergency plan, then collects crew signatures. The safety record can later be filtered, reviewed, printed, and retained independently from production billing.

slides.title: Storm Mode
slides.script: Storm Mode applies only to crews selected by the Administrator. The Admin creates the event and assigns participating crews. New daily reports from those crews receive the storm tag automatically. Crews that remain on normal construction continue in regular mode. This separation supports accurate storm billing, payroll, readiness tracking, filtering, and event-specific exports.

slides.title: Reporting, Review, and Audit
slides.script: Submitted reports enter a review queue. Managers can filter by job, Foreman, date, status, exceptions, crew, and storm event. They can inspect units, attachments, report history, and financial summaries before approving or returning work. Printed P D F reports and filtered C S V exports support office workflows, customer documentation, payroll, billing, and closeout.

slides.title: Foreman Guide
slides.script: This section covers the Foreman's complete daily workflow: morning safety, report creation, pole-by-pole unit entry, exception checking, submission, and storm work when assigned.

slides.title: Foreman Responsibilities
slides.script: A Foreman owns the field record. Complete the morning JSA before work. Record the correct job, hours, weather, delays, poles, units, work types, and quantities. Review the report before submission. New company members begin as Foremen. Foremen see the company's field value, which may be adjusted below actual contract pricing by the Administrator.

slides.title: Complete the Morning JSA
slides.script: Open Safety and Morning JSA from the dashboard. Select the correct job and crew, then verify the date and location. Enter the planned work, hazards, controls, P P E, and emergency information. Brief the crew and collect each required signature. Save the JSA and confirm it appears in the safety list before production begins.

slides.title: Create the Daily Report
slides.script: At the end of the workday, open Production and choose Create Daily Report. Select the correct job and work date. Confirm the Foreman and crew. Enter regular hours, overtime, weather, delays, delay hours, and notes. Save the report as a draft, then open Manage Units. The report remains editable until it is submitted for review.

slides.title: Enter Units Efficiently
slides.script: Enter one pole or work point, then add every completed unit at that location. Start typing the actual unit code whenever possible, choose the matching contract unit, select Install or Remove and enter the exact quantity. Choose Save Pole and Add Next, then repeat for the next pole. Completed poles remain available in the compact review list.

slides.title: Verify and Submit
slides.script: Before submission, inspect each saved line. Authorized entries match the packet. Pending entries are allowed but await a later packet. Redlines require management review. Correct any mistaken pole, unit, work type, or quantity while the report is still a draft. Select Done Adding Units, review the full report, and then Submit Report.

slides.title: Foreman Storm Workflow
slides.script: When your crew is assigned to an active storm, confirm the orange Storm Mode banner and event name. Create the daily report normally. The system applies the event tag automatically. Record hours, delays, poles, and units exactly as completed, then verify the Storm label before submission. Administrators—not Foremen—control which crews participate in the event.

slides.title: General Foreman Guide
slides.script: This section explains how a General Foreman reviews crews, resolves production exceptions, approves or returns reports, and monitors job progress across the company.

slides.title: General Foreman Responsibilities
slides.script: The General Foreman manages operational quality across crews. Work the submitted-report queue, compare field records to authorized work, review pending and redline entries, and monitor job completion. General Foremen can see actual and adjusted values when both exist. They should return inaccurate reports with clear instructions instead of silently changing the Foreman's record.

slides.title: Work the Review Queue
slides.script: Open Production from the dashboard or use the Production Needs Review shortcut. Use filters to narrow reports by status, job, Foreman, crew, date, exception type, or completion stage. Expand a compact row, open View Units, and compare the job, hours, notes, pole locations, quantities, values, attachments, and history before making a decision.

slides.title: Approve, Return, and Resolve Redlines
slides.script: Confirm that authorized entries match the packet and investigate pending entries. For redlines, verify that the added or over-quantity work is legitimate and documented. Approve a complete and accurate report. Return an incorrect report with a specific reason. If the company requires General Foreman approval for redlines, that review must occur before final Admin approval.

slides.title: Monitor Jobs Across Crews
slides.script: Use Active Job Progress to compare authorized, reported, approved, and remaining value. Reported work can be ahead of approved work while reports wait in the queue. Filter by job or crew to manage higher volume. Redline and pending counts highlight items that could affect billing. Exports provide a clean handoff to operations and office staff.

slides.title: Administrator Guide
slides.script: This section covers the Administrator's full system responsibility: company setup, user roles, contracts, pricing, imports, utility packets, approvals, reporting, storm configuration, and secure support tools.

slides.title: Administrator Responsibilities
slides.script: Administrators control the business foundation. They configure the company, invite users, promote roles, manage commercial pricing, create jobs, import utility packages, review production, configure storm events, and produce exports. Admin access also includes governance responsibilities such as company isolation, audit history, approval policy, and controlled handling of API credentials.

slides.title: Set Up Company and Team
slides.script: Enter the company display name, time zone, contact details, logo, and brand color. Share the company join code only with approved people. New members enter as Foremen. Promote selected people to General Foreman or Admin. Configure whether redline reports require General Foreman approval, and assign job leaders where responsibility needs to be visible.

slides.title: Build Contracts and Pricing
slides.script: Create the customer or utility, then create its contract with the correct number and dates. Set a field-value adjustment if Foremen should see a percentage below actual pricing. Create a price book under that contract, import and verify the units, and activate the correct version. Duplicate the book before future revisions so historical pricing remains intact.

slides.title: Import a Utility Job Packet
slides.script: Open the correct job and add a utility package with its reference, received date, and notes. Choose the spreadsheet, select the proper worksheet, and map work point, description, unit code, work type, and quantity columns. Preview the rows and correct invalid mappings. Nothing saves until the Administrator confirms the import.

slides.title: Reconcile, Approve, and Report
slides.script: When a late packet is imported, the system compares earlier production using company, job, normalized work point, and unit code. Entries then become Authorized or Redline. Follow the General Foreman approval policy and document any Admin override. Monitor reported and approved completion, review attachments and history, then export or archive records for billing and closeout.

slides.title: Configure Storm Operations
slides.script: Create the storm event and define its operational details. Select only the participating crews and verify readiness before work begins. Normal crews remain in standard mode. Monitor storm-tagged reports by event and crew, then use event-specific exports and summaries for management, payroll, and billing.

slides.title: Admin Helper and Secure AI
slides.script: The current Admin Helper explains features and common workflows. The planned secure AI layer will provide context-aware guidance, diagnostics, and onboarding assistance for Administrators only. API calls must run through a protected server-side service. The secret key must never be placed in the public GitHub Pages JavaScript or exposed to Foreman and General Foreman accounts.

slides.title: Daily Operating Rhythm
slides.script: The complete rhythm is straightforward. The Foreman starts with the morning JSA, leads the work, records production, and submits the daily report. The General Foreman reviews the field record and resolves exceptions. The Administrator controls commercial data, policy, final oversight, storm configuration, and reporting. Together, these steps create safer work, accurate quantities, controlled approvals, and defensible billing.
